item.title: UK announces sanctions on West Bank settlements prompting furious Israeli response
item.description:
The Trump administration did not oppose a UK-led initiative to impose new sanctions on Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, U.S. officials and Western diplomats say. Why it matters: The White House's decision not to push back on the UK effort, which 11 other Western countries have joined, is a signal of its frustration with the Netanyahu government's policy in the West Bank. Driving the news: The UK announced Tuesday it would impose sanctions against individuals and entities involved in building settlements in the West Bank. The UK also announced a ban on imported goods from the Israeli settlements. The move came in response to the Netanyahu government's decision to move forward with a new settlement in the sensitive E1 area, which would divide the West Bank and prevent territorial contiguity in any future Palestinian state. item.title: Mamdani releases 170,000 pages of records regarding impact on air quality of 9/11 attacks
item.description:
New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani speaks during a press conference on the release of 9/11 related documents at City Hall on Sept. 8, 2026, in New York City. —Michael M. Santiago—Getty Images As the 25th anniversary of the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks in New York City approaches, Mayor Zohran Mamdani has launched a portal giving the public access to about 170,000 pages of documents concerning air quality, health hazards, and the government’s response following 9/11. Its long-sought documents, which had previously been kept out of the public eye, show that New York City leaders were aware of the dangers posed by toxic contamination around Ground Zero following the attacks, even while they continued to tell New Yorkers that the air was safe to breathe. Some of the pages were reportedly found in 68 boxes stashed in a city office, which advocates argue had been kept away from the public for years…

item.title: US envoys Witkoff and Kushner hold Ukraine talks after meeting Putin
item.description:
President Trump's envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Kyiv on Sunday for diplomatic talks aimed at resuming negotiations between Russia and Ukraine . Why it matters: Kushner and Witkoff traveled to Kyiv right after talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow. This is Witkoff and Kushner's first trip to Ukraine despite months of negotiating with both sides and multiple trips to Russia. Sunday also marked the highest-level visit by a U.S. official to Ukraine since Trump started his second term. Driving the news: U.S. and Russian officials offered positive assessments of Kushner and Witkoff's three-hour meeting with Putin on Saturday. "Kushner and Witkoff are making an effort, and we are making progress," a Russian official said. A White House official said Witkoff, Kushner and Putin discussed "plans for next steps, which will be announced in the coming weeks."…

item.title: French police hunt Renoir thieves after lightning museum heist
item.description:
The Renoir Museum’s alarms went off at 5:48 a.m., but by the time police arrived 5 minutes later, it was already too late — two paintings had been stolen. The thieves broke into the museum on Tuesday, located in the French city of Cagnes-sur-Mer, by cutting through a fence and entering through the main floor, according to the Associated Press . The thieves then cut the bolts holding the four paintings in place and managed to get away with two of the four paintings. Two paintings were left behind in the garden during their escape. Mayor Bryan Masson later revealed that the two stolen artworks are “Portrait of Madame Colonna Romano” and “Young Woman at the Well.” The two abandoned paintings — “Coco Lisant” and “Portrait of Madame Pichon”— were recovered. item.title: Democrats need to win. Here’s the message our research says works
item.description:
Guest Commentary written by Dave Vorland Dave Vorland leads the Blue Horizon Project at Chamber of Progress. He has served in the Obama and Biden administrations and worked in space and missile defense policy. Democrats have long been the party of innovation. John F. Kennedy promised the moon. Bill Clinton and Al Gore embraced the internet revolution. Barack Obama saw technology as a force that could improve lives and modernize government. When HealthCare.gov failed, Obama didn’t declare war on technologists. He brought them in to fix it. item.description:
Farewell, New Mexico. The war isn’t going well and nowhere on Earth is safe from the US president’s favourite displacement activity Busy times for crayon-wielding US president Donald Trump, Earth’s most tireless freelance cartographer, who at the weekend celebrated the US labouring under the highest diesel prices in its history while his “two-week” Iran war edges into its seventh month with a social media spree in which he pushed renaming New Mexico as New America. item.title: Israel's Netanyahu denies UAE warned him of October 7 attack
item.description:
Israeli opposition leaders on Tuesday called Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu unfit to serve after a report that the United Arab Emirates had warned him before the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack. Haaretz newspaper, in a report excerpted from a forthcoming book by its reporters, said UAE President Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan spoke to Netanyahu a week and a half before the attack and told him that Hamas was planning a major operation. FRANCE 24's Monte Francis reports.
